kinds.d: Rug or mat with a mihrab niche, made to kneel, stand or prostrate on in prayer. A meditation cushion or mat is in Soft Furnishings.

x.d: Balanced geometric and floral design, mihrab single, double or multiplied, symmetrical Ghiordes knot.
Graceful mihrab with realistic floral decoration, often a Tree of Life; finer asymmetrical Senneh knot.
x.dt: wool or silk · Tree of Life

x.d: Flat-woven cotton prayer rug; 18th-century Bijapur cotton rugs show domed minarets in the mihrab.

kinds.d: String of 33, 99 or 101 beads with a divider and tassel, made to count Muslim dhikr; sold in wood, stone, seed and resin and as 33-bead bracelets.

x.d: Usually 100 beads in three groups (33, 33, 34) separated by two imam beads, with a yad handle.
x.dt: wood, olive seed, amber, onyx, carnelian

x.d: Prayer beads of faturan, a cast phenol-formaldehyde resin made by Traun and Son of Hamburg until the 1940s; vintage strands are collected.

kinds.d: Folding X-shaped stand for holding the Qur'an during recitation.

x.d: Light green nephrite Qur'an stand from Mughal India, 19th century, in the LACMA collection.

kinds.d: Case or cover made to hold and protect a copy of the Qur'an, from miniature armband cases to boxes.

x.d: Box for a miniature Qur'an that can be strapped to the arm, of engraved steel inlaid with gold wire.

kinds.d: Compass with city marks or a second pointer to find the direction of Mecca.

x.d: Round brass box with hinged lid, inset compass, glass cover and folding gnomon, sites listed in Arabic.

kinds.d: Metal and glass lantern hung in homes and streets in Ramadan; an Egyptian tradition now across the Muslim world.

x.d: Egyptian folk lantern traced to medieval Cairo and the welcome of the Fatimid caliph al-Muizz.

kinds.d: Framed Qur'anic or devotional calligraphy made for the home.

x.d: Bold, large-scale script made for panels and inscriptions read at a distance.
Calligraphic artwork describing the Prophet's physical and moral qualities, hung on walls.

traditions.d: Rugs woven with a mihrab niche in regional styles, from Ottoman geometry to Persian florals.
traditions.tech: knotted pile (Ghiordes and Senneh knots) or flat weave
traditions.auth: Knot type and mihrab layout identify the tradition.
